Name: Tusa Hiti
Description: natural landmark tusa hiti also known a tusha hiti or tusha hit is a historic stone spout located in lalitpur nepal spout like tusa hiti are traditional water source that have been an integral part of the kathmandu valley urban infrastructure for century providing clean water for drinking bathing and religious ritual tusa hiti is believed to have been constructed during the malla period which lasted from the 12th to the 18th century the malla ruler known for their patronage of art architecture and culture commissioned the construction of many public amenity including stone spout like tusa hiti a a way to serve the need of the local population

Name: Ugrachandi Mandir Patan
Description: religious site the charming ugrachandi mandir which is also known a tamakhdyah lie in the local tole of patan this square fourstorey temple with a hip roof made of flat sheet ha an air of mystery the first recorded mention of the temple is from 1702 ce but it true age is not known inside the temple house the fierce goddess ugrachandi the mother deity of the tamrakar clan hence this give the temple it newar name tamakahdyah which mean the goddess of tamkrakars according to legend she wa brought from kathmandu to patan through tantric magic the goddess is still revered in this modern age despite holding it ancient religious value many physical change have been added to this ancient site in 1756 and 1761 a beautiful wooden torana wa added to the temple today an iconic stone under a copper torana in the sanctum represents ugrachandi exuding divine peace the divinity of this temple is kept alive by various ritual and worship a newar upadhyaya brahmin conduct daily ritual supported by the tamrakar community various tamkrakar guthi local newari community involve themselves by sponsoring different religious event at this temple among these event key activity of the shrine include the regular ugrachandi worship this occurs between the full moon of the month baishakh and the sixth day of the brighter half of the month jestha here also occurs the grand tahguthi puha with animal sacrifice and a community feast these vibrant ritual and ceremony breathe life into the temple making it not just a structure of stone and wood but a living symbol of the tamrakar people faith and culture

Name: Uma Maheshwor Temple Kirtipur
Description: religious site it is said that bishwo nath source from patan made endowment to built this temple and installed idol of bhawani shankar which is now known a bhawani shankar uma maheshwor the idol wa installed in respect of shiva and his concort parvati both immensely worshipped by hindusinside the temple inscription dated 1662 ad 1678 ad 1679 ad 1687 ad 1715 ad 782 n 798 n 779 n 807 n and 835 n can be found idol of saraswati maheshmardini and ganesh are also placed inside temple architectural characteristic the temple stoods a an example of extraordinary newah temple architecture this three tiered temple rest on a raised platform of four successive plinth made of bricka stone stairway lead to ground floor of temple where a circumambulatory space is also provided in the form of verandah two elephant in the first plinth guard the entry way inner core brickwall and twenty number of beautifully carved exterior column support the upper structure just below the first roof a verandah like space is provided instead of solid wall normally seen in other templesthe brick wall are provided with decorated door and window all the three roof are finished with jhingati tile and supported from below by decorative timber strut the strut consists of image of godsgoddesses the temple is topped by metal gajur and a metal banner is hanged down from gajur to first tier in the front side a uma maheshwor temple is located in high elevation it provides the good view of kathmandu and immediate surroundings

Name: Baluwakhani (Pashupati Kshetra Vikash Kosh)
Description: baluwakhani situated within the pashupati area in kageshwari manohara nepal is a historic site renowned for it cultural and religious significance a part of the pashupatinath temple complex a unesco world heritage site it offer visitor a profound insight into nepal rich heritage historical and cultural significance pashupatinath temple complex the pashupatinath temple dedicated to lord shiva is one of the most sacred hindu temple globally the temple complex span 246 hectare and includes 518 minitemples and ashram along the bank of the sacred bagmati river unesco world heritage site designated in 1979 the pashupatinath temple complex is recognized for it extensive collection of temple ashram image and inscription reflecting century of religious and cultural development visitor experience spiritual atmosphere visitor can immerse themselves in the spiritual ambiance of the area observing traditional hindu ritual and ceremony that are regularly performed architectural marvel the site feature traditional pagodastyle architecture intricate wood carving and sacred symbol offering a visual feast for those interested in historical structure cultural observation the bagmati river flowing through the complex is a significant site for hindu cremation ceremony providing visitor with a deeper understanding of local custom and belief practical information location baluwakhani is located within the pashupati area in kageshwari manohara approximately 5 kilometer northeast of kathmandu city center visiting hour the temple complex is generally open to visitor from early morning until late evening however certain area may have restricted access during specific ritual or festival entry requirement while the inner sanctum of the pashupatinath temple is reserved for hindu the surrounding premise are open to visitor of all background modest attire and respectful behavior are expected

Name: Barahi Ajima Temple
Description: the barahi ajima temple also known a yakati ajima in nepalbhasa is a significant religious site located in bhaktapur nepal situated near the araniko highway just west of the suryabinayak crossing this temple hold substantial cultural and spiritual importance for the local community historical and cultural significance barahi ajima is revered a the female counterpart of lord vishnu boar incarnation lord baraha according to local tradition the goddess barahi wa created on the fifth day of nawaratri a festival dedicated to the worship of the nine form of the goddess durga the temple is part of the astamatrika mandala which encompasses eight mother goddess and is integral to the nawaratri celebration in bhaktapur architectural feature the temple showcase traditional newari architecture characterized by intricate wood carving and a tiered pagodastyle roof it proximity to the araniko highway make it easily accessible to visitor festival and ritual during nawaratri devotee flock to the temple to offer prayer and seek blessing the temple also host various ceremony including the preparation of samay baji—a traditional newari ritual platter—during special occasion visitor experience visitor to the barahi ajima temple can immerse themselves in the rich cultural heritage of bhaktapur the temple serene environment coupled with the vibrant local tradition offer a unique experience for those interested in nepalese culture and spirituality
